system-user.title: Users
system-user.description: User list, creation, status changes and deletion against the new iam/users endpoints. The level model is gone; ownership is expressed through departments.
system-user.scopeSuperAdminTitle: Signed in as a platform-level account
system-user.scopeSuperAdmin: The session carries no tenant, so no tenant filter is offered. List scope and creatable departments are still decided upstream; this page only avoids entry points that hit known gaps.
system-user.scopeTenantAdminTitle: Signed in as a tenant-level account
system-user.scopeTenantAdmin: The session carries a tenant, so the upstream limits the list to what you may see; cross-tenant operations are rejected upstream.
system-user.scopeUnknownTitle: Signed in as an unknown identity
system-user.scopeUnknown: The session has no user info yet (signed out or still loading). The list scope is whatever the upstream returns; this page infers nothing.
system-user.keywordPlaceholder: Search username, display name or email
system-user.detailEmpty: Select a user on the left to see the details

system-user.immutableHint: The username is fixed once created; display name, email and department can be updated through PUT /iam/users/{id}, and the department carries the tenant.

statusModal.disableHint: A disabled user cannot sign in but the record stays; use delete to remove it entirely.
statusModal.deleteHint: This is a soft delete (deleted_at): the account leaves the list and can no longer sign in. It cannot be undone from this page.

system-log.title: Audit log
system-log.description: Audit log: operation logs, security logs and archive records in one page. The upstream decides the data scope from the caller's identity (a super admin sees the whole platform, a tenant admin only their tenant; filtering happens upstream), and the page spells out which scope you are looking at.
system-log.empty: No records of this kind yet
system-log.emptyFiltered: No records match the current filters
system-log.loadFailed: Could not load the audit log
system-log.detailFailed: Could not load the record detail
system-log.selectHint: Pick a record on the left to see its detail

filter.title: Filters
filter.reversed: The start time is later than the end time: the upstream returns an empty set for a reversed range, so adjust it first.

scope.title: What you can see
scope.superAdmin: A super admin sees the whole platform's audit log and can run archiving. The authorisation decision still happens upstream (NMCPS-ADR-0018).
scope.tenantAdmin: A tenant admin sees the log after the upstream filters it by tenant (only actions of accounts in this tenant). Data outside the scope never shows up here, and there is no cross-tenant switch.
scope.shape: The entry fields of operation and security logs have not been verified against real data yet (the audit tables of the test instance are empty, see NMCPS-REC-004 UP-AUD-10): the page renders the registered fields only, shows an em dash for missing ones, and lists any unregistered field as-is at the end of the detail. Archive records were verified and are not affected.

archive.hint: Move expired entries into the archive tables using the upstream retention window (a write, cannot be undone)
archive.title: Run archive
archive.description: Archiving moves expired rows of both log tables into the archive tables following the upstream retention window, and leaves one batch record behind. It is a write operation and cannot be undone.
archive.warning: Only rows older than the retention cutoff are moved: when nothing has expired the result is 0 rows, which is a normal outcome, not a failure.

system-permission.title: Permissions
system-permission.description: Role CRUD plus policy-by-role grants. The upstream has no permission-point catalogue (gap G3): actions live inside policy documents, so authorisation is a policy checklist rather than permission switches.
system-permission.emptySearch: No roles match the current filter
system-permission.detailEmpty: Select a role on the left
system-permission.detailEmptyHint: The list and the detail share this page; on narrow screens selecting a role opens the detail and Back returns to the list.
system-permission.selectionMissingTitle: That role is not in the current results
system-permission.selectionMissing: “{id}” from the link is not part of the current filter / page. To keep the filter and the address bar consistent, the page will not page through results to find it.
system-permission.loadFailed: Failed to load the role list
system-permission.systemHintTitle: System role: a label, not a protection
system-permission.systemHint: is_system is only a semantic label: the upstream happily accepts grants, renames and deletes (UP-RBAC-02). A deleted seed role can only be restored by changing the database.
system-permission.customHint: Grants and members apply one by one with no Save button; a revoke has to be redone by hand.
system-permission.scopePlatform: Sees platform roles plus every tenant role; new roles land in tnt_default (the request body has no tenant_id, UP-RBAC-08).
system-permission.scopeTenant: Sees this tenant's roles plus templates assigned by the platform; new objects land in this tenant. The new generation has no business-level authorisation: visibility depends only on the session tenant (UP-RBAC-01).
system-permission.scopeUnknownTitle: Signed in as: session not ready
system-permission.scopeUnknown: The session tenant is unavailable. The page still loads (the upstream does not reject by identity), but which tenant a write lands in is decided server-side.

form.description: All three fields are required client-side: the upstream validates nothing and an empty body creates an empty role (UP-RBAC-07).
form.editDescription: The role code cannot change after creation; only name and description are written. enabled is ignored upstream (UP-RBAC-03), so there is no on/off switch.
form.name: Role name
form.codeHint: 2–64 chars: letters, digits, underscore, dot and hyphen only; cannot change after creation
form.codeImmutable: Cannot change after creation (PUT ignores the field)
form.descriptionPlaceholder: Optional: what this role is for

deleteModal.title: Delete role
deleteModal.description: Deleting {name} also drops its attached policies and assigned users.
deleteModal.systemTitle: System roles are deleted just the same
deleteModal.systemHint: The upstream does not protect is_system: DELETE on a seed role returns success too (UP-RBAC-02), and there is no restore endpoint.
deleteModal.hint: The upstream has no restore endpoint: deletion is final, a role has to be recreated and re-granted.

policies.title: Granted policies
policies.hint: Checking attaches (AttachPolicy) and unchecking detaches (DetachPolicy); each change applies immediately, there is no Save button.
policies.empty: The upstream returned no visible policies
policies.orphanHint: Hidden relation rows: {count}, pointing at policies that no longer exist (UP-RBAC-10); refreshing will not clean them up.

members.title: Assigned users
members.hint: Read, assign and revoke only; create accounts in User management. Assign and revoke apply immediately.
members.empty: No user is assigned to this role yet
members.orphanHint: Hidden relation rows: {count}, pointing at users that no longer exist (UP-RBAC-10).

system-policy.title: Policies
system-policy.description: Create, edit and delete policies (iam/policies) and preview their documents: visibility follows the session tenant, while enable/disable and document editing have no entry point.
system-policy.detailEmpty: Select a policy on the left to see its details
system-policy.detailEmptyHint: The list and the detail pane are two columns of the same page; on narrow screens selecting a policy opens the detail and Back returns to the list.
system-policy.selectionMissingTitle: That policy is not in the current result
system-policy.selectionMissing: The id in the link ({id}) is not on the current page. The page will not silently fetch another page, because that would desync the filters and the URL.
system-policy.loadFailed: Failed to load the policy list
system-policy.copyFailed: Copy failed: the browser denied clipboard access
system-policy.documentInvalidHint: This is not valid JSON: the upstream stores it as jsonb and will reject it on write.
system-policy.documentHint: The upstream performs no policy-syntax validation: storing it does not mean it is correct, so the page only formats it for reading and never claims it is validated.
system-policy.documentReadonly: Policy documents have no editor (a broken document is dirty data): change them through the upstream API or a data-correction process.
system-policy.scopePlatform: Policies of every tenant are visible; new policies land in the default tenant tnt_default (the request body does not accept tenant_id).
system-policy.scopeTenant: Visibility is decided by the session tenant alone: the new generation has no business-level authorisation, so any authenticated session (including role-less accounts) can read and write these endpoints (NMCPS-REC-005 UP-RBAC-01).
system-policy.scopeUnknown: The session is not ready: sign in before managing policies. The upstream decides on the token alone, and this page adds no client-side gate.

form.description: Name, code and document are required client-side; the upstream validates neither required fields nor the code format, and the document is only checked for being parseable JSON.
form.editDescription: Only name and description can change: policy code and document are immutable after creation, and the document is resubmitted as-is.
form.name: Policy name
form.codeHint: Unique per tenant (reusable across tenants); letters, digits, underscore, hyphen and dot only
form.codeImmutable: The code cannot change after creation (the upstream PUT does not accept it)
form.policyTypeHint: The upstream does not constrain the enum (every seeded row is system); defaults to custom
form.policyTypeImmutable: The type cannot change after creation
form.documentHint: Must be valid JSON; the upstream stores it as jsonb and rejects invalid JSON
form.documentReadonly: The document is resubmitted as-is; this page does not edit it.

deleteModal.title: Delete policy
deleteModal.hint: Deleting cannot be undone; a policy still attached to roles leaves orphan rows in the relation resource that must be cleaned up separately.
deleteModal.systemTitle: The upstream does not protect system policies
deleteModal.systemHint: is_system is only a label: a measured DELETE on a system policy succeeds, and the row is neither recoverable nor recreated automatically.

user-security.mfaCodeInvalid: Wrong one-time code, check the authenticator clock and retry
user-security.passwordHint: The current session stays valid; if the upstream revokes tokens afterwards, the next request refreshes automatically.

user-security.newPasswordSame: The new password must differ from the current one
user-security.confirmPasswordMismatch: The two passwords do not match
